description:
Project: Auto-rollback on SLO breach integration

Goal
- Make Redwood’s rollout controller capable of automatically rolling back a model/version when production latency and/or error-rate SLOs breach configurable thresholds.
- Reduce MTTR and customer impact during bad rollouts (runtime regressions, misconfigurations, capacity/region anomalies) while preventing rollback “flapping.”

Scope (in)
- Wire Rollout Controller (control plane) to SLO monitors (latency + error) via standardized monitor identities and query templates (per route/model/customer tier/region).
- Configurable rollback policies: threshold values, evaluation windows, minimum traffic, cooldowns, and “must-be-worse-than-baseline” comparisons.
- Rollback actions: revert canary/AB traffic split to prior stable version; emit audit log + event stream; notify Slack/on-call.
- Console support: view policy, current health verdict, rollback history, and manual override/ack.
- Reliability hardening: guardrails against false positives (low traffic, deploy warm-up), and safe behavior under monitoring outages (fail-open vs fail-closed policy).
- Testing: synthetic SLO breach tests, game day, staged rollout, and post-launch alert tuning.

Non-goals (out)
- Building a full new monitoring system; project relies on existing telemetry/observability pipelines and dashboards.
- Automatically rolling forward to a new candidate (“auto-remediation beyond rollback”).
- Quality (LLM output) regressions; this project focuses on latency/error SLOs (quality gates remain separate).

Key stakeholders / teams
- Product: Marissa Cole (Dir PM, Console & Rollouts), Paula Mendes (Sr PM, rollout policies)
- Platform Control Plane: Ethan Park (EM), Benji Okafor (SSE), Jordan Lee (policy engine)
- Telemetry/Observability: Logan Wright (EM), Nadia Rahman (Staff), Allison Grant (Observability)
- SRE/On-call: Sean Gallagher (Dir SRE), Rafael Mendes (SRE Mgr), Miles Thornton (Staff SRE)
- Console Backend: Chloe Martin (EM), Jada Williams (Staff)
- Release Engineering: Connor O’Brien

Constraints and risks
- Signal quality: SLO calculation latency, metric cardinality, and region/model labeling consistency.
- False positives: low-volume routes, canary warm-up, and correlated incidents (e.g., upstream network) triggering unnecessary rollback.
- Rollback safety: must avoid cascading rollbacks across many tenants simultaneously; include rate limiting and per-tenant guardrails.
- Compliance/audit: rollback actions must be attributable and visible (audit log + change history).

Deliverables
- Confluence PRD + design spec + ADRs (policy semantics, monitor identity contract).
- Implementation across control plane, telemetry/observability, and console.
- Runbooks + game day plan.
- Linear project with tracked dependencies; GitHub PR set across `redwood` and observability repos.

Timeline (typical 6–8 weeks)
- Week 1–2: PRD + design review; define monitor identity + SLO query templates; spike implementation.
- Week 3–5: Implement policy evaluation + rollback executor; observability wiring; console views; audit log events.
- Week 6: Integration tests + perf checks; game day; staged rollout to internal + low-risk tenants.
- Week 7–8: General availability; post-launch tuning; docs/runbook polish.

files.description: PRD: user problems, target customers/tiers, success metrics (rollback time, incident reduction), UX requirements, rollout plan, and non-goals.
Technical design spec: architecture, policy model, monitor contracts, evaluation algorithm, rollback executor, failure modes, and data model changes.
ADR defining canonical monitor identity (labels/tags) for latency/error SLOs across route/model/region/tier; includes examples and migration plan.
ADR for policy semantics: windows, burn-rate vs fixed threshold, cooldowns, minimum traffic, baseline comparisons, and fail-open/fail-closed behavior.
Service doc update: rollout-controller components, new SLO-evaluator module, dependencies on telemetry/monitoring, and operational limits.
SRE-facing doc enumerating the exact latency and error SLO definitions used for rollback decisions, including tiered SLOs and exclusions.
Dashboard/alert specification: required panels, alert thresholds, paging vs ticketing guidance, and links used by automated rollback.
Runbook: how auto-rollback triggers, how to pause/override, how to validate monitor correctness, and step-by-step mitigation workflow.
Game day plan: scenarios (latency regression, 5xx spike, monitor outage), success criteria, roles, comms plan, and follow-up checklist.
Postmortem that motivates the feature: timeline, impact, why rollback didn’t happen fast enough, action items feeding into this project.
Audit logging spec: event types for policy changes, automated rollback trigger, executor actions, and who/what initiated changes.
CI/testing doc: synthetic SLO breach harness, integration tests across control plane + telemetry, and canary verification steps.
Working PRD notes: open questions, customer anecdotes, proposed defaults, and trade-offs before Confluence PRD finalization.
Sheet: proposed query templates, required metric labels, example time windows, and a checklist for monitor creation per service/route.
Spike notes: feasibility of consuming monitors, API options, caching strategy, rate limits, and early prototype results.
SRE workbook: initial threshold proposals, false-positive analysis, paging policy, and a tuning plan after launch.
Launch checklist: feature flag plan, staged rollout cohorts, rollback plan for the feature itself, comms templates, and sign-offs.
PM personal notes: customer feedback snippets and prioritized requirements (e.g., per-tenant thresholds, cooldowns, visibility/audit needs).
Top-level Linear project brief: milestones, scope boundaries, success metrics, and cross-team dependencies.
Implement monitor consumption client and caching layer in rollout controller; includes acceptance criteria and error handling.
Define config schema (per route/model/region/tier), migration strategy, and validation rules for rollback policies.
Choose and implement evaluation algorithm; compare fixed thresholds vs burn-rate; include testing plan and guardrails.
Executor implementation with idempotency keys, per-tenant throttling, and safe handling of repeated breach events.
Console backend endpoints: verdict state, timeline of breaches, actions taken, and policy display; includes pagination and auth.
Emit audit events for policy change + auto-rollback trigger + action; includes event schema and compliance review checklist.
Add internal metrics: evaluator lag, monitor fetch errors, number of rollbacks by cause, and false-positive counters.
Create runbook links in alerts; ensure oncall routing; define when to page vs create ticket for auto-rollback events.
End-to-end test harness to simulate latency/error spikes and verify rollback; includes CI gating criteria.
Define gating flags, rollout cohorts, and criteria to expand rollout; includes rollback plan for the feature.
Migrate existing monitors to the new identity contract; includes backfill scripts and validation dashboards.
Plan and execute the game day; capture outcomes, issues found, and follow-up tasks.
PR: Add SLO monitor client to rollout-controller service; includes caching, retries, and rate limiting.
PR: Introduce rollback policy schema + config validation; includes migration notes and backwards compatibility.
PR: Implement SLO evaluator (windowing, thresholds, cooldown) and decision trace logging.
PR: Rollback executor with idempotency and safe traffic-split revert; includes integration with routing config.
PR: Emit audit log events for policy changes and automated rollback actions.
PR: Console backend APIs for rollout health verdict + rollback history; includes authz checks and pagination.
PR: Add internal metrics (evaluator lag, monitor fetch errors, rollbacks by cause) and update dashboards wiring.
PR: Integration tests for synthetic SLO breach; adds CI job and flake reduction work.
PR: Add standardized dashboards/panels for rollout SLOs (latency + error) and alert templates referenced by controller.
PR: Add reusable SLO query templates and label normalization helpers for route/model/region/tier.
PR: Add notification type for automated rollback events (Slack message formatting, links to runbook and rollout page).
PR (hotfix-style): Guardrail to prevent rollback when monitor is stale/unavailable; introduces explicit ‘unknown’ verdict handling.
Thread: control plane team debating policy defaults (min traffic, warm-up windows) and how to represent them in config.
